recent_posts.title: [GSoC 2026] Bluetooth: HCI Improvements & HID Profile | Haiku Project
recent_posts.summary: Mohammed R. Attia introduces his GSoC 2026 project with Haiku OS: modernizing the Bluetooth stack and implementing the HID profile. The project covers three main areas: completing missing HCI commands (inquiry, pairing, link key persistence, disconnection handling), implementing an SDP client for service discovery, and building a working HID Bluetooth profile to support keyboards and mice. The goal is to make Haiku's Bluetooth stack functional with modern devices end-to-end.

recent_posts.title: [GSoC 2026] Modernizing Haiku’s Bluetooth stack: Implementing support for HFP profile
recent_posts.summary: A GSoC 2026 project proposal to modernize Haiku OS's Bluetooth stack by implementing the Hands-Free Profile (HFP). The work involves adding SCO (Synchronous Connection-Oriented) link support for low-latency audio, RFCOMM protocol support, Serial Port Profile, and finally the HFP profile itself. Completion will allow Haiku users to use Bluetooth headphones and earphones for audio and voice calls.

recent_posts.title: Haiku to mentor 3 students in Google Summer of Code 2026
recent_posts.summary: Haiku OS has been accepted into Google Summer of Code 2026 and will mentor 3 students. Aquamatic will work on expanding the Devices application, while Mohammed R. Attia and Vighnesh Sawant will collaborate on improving Bluetooth support — Mohammed focusing on HID devices (mice and keyboards) and Vighnesh on HFP and audio support.

recent_posts.title: Haiku Activity & Contract Report, March 2026 (ft. ARM64)
recent_posts.summary: Monthly development report for the Haiku OS project covering March 2026 (hrev59431–hrev59569). The headline item is significant progress on the ARM64 port, which can now reach the desktop in QEMU thanks to contributors smrobtzz and SED4906. Other highlights include: major kernel SMP message logic overhauls and VM/swap improvements by waddlesplash; Hyper-V driver work by Goldfish64; Bluetooth server fixes and pairing support; BFS locking bug fixes; package state auto-cleanup in pkgman; SSL certificate validation fixes; and numerous application-level improvements across Tracker, WebPositive, Mail, and more. The beta6 release is not yet ready due to remaining WebPositive bugs.

recent_posts.title: Haiku Activity & Contract Report, February 2026
recent_posts.summary: Monthly development report for the Haiku OS project covering hrev59356 through hrev59430. Key changes include: Mail app gains 'labels' feature replacing custom statuses; Deskbar gets a location selector UI; BGeolocation switches from discontinued Mozilla Location Service to Beacon DB; virtio_block driver disabled due to multithreading bugs; EHCI USB2 zero-copy optimization disabled after causing crashes; BTRFS gains Zstd-compressed file reading; XFS driver gets multiple fixes; Hyper-V VMbus driver added by a new contributor; pthread_barrier reworked to fix OpenGL hangs; TLB invalidation optimized on x86; and several filesystem crash fixes across NTFS, BFS, FAT, and RAMFS. Beta 6 release is getting closer but blocked by a kernel memory accounting regression under review and 5-6 remaining bugs.

recent_posts.title: Haiku to mentor interns in Google Summer of Code 2026
recent_posts.summary: Haiku OS has been accepted as a mentoring organization for Google Summer of Code 2026. New contributors will work on improving Haiku and related applications over the summer, supported by a mentor team and a Google-provided stipend. The participant application window opens March 16, with coding running from late May through August (optionally until October). A list of project ideas is available for prospective applicants.

recent_posts.title: Haiku Activity & Contract Report, January 2026
recent_posts.summary: Haiku OS development in January 2026 included improvements to file panels and drag-and-drop, enhanced MIME handling in Tracker, disk image support in DriveSetup, and touchpad functionality with two-finger scrolling. Networking received IPv6 support in telnet and netstat, plus Path MTU discovery. The kernel gained POSIX compliance fixes, improved timezone handling, and new system calls from POSIX-2024. File systems saw BFS query optimizations and write_overlay fixes. Build system updates synchronized packages with HaikuPorts and introduced unit test automation infrastructure. Progress continues toward beta6 release.

recent_posts.title: The Gerrit code review iceberg, episode 5
recent_posts.summary: The Haiku OS project reviews five stalled code changes from 2021 in their Gerrit system. The pending changes include a DeskBar location menu (needs better UI approach), StyledEdit window naming (localization issues), GCC warning suppression (should fix code instead), Wacom tablet support (incomplete), and VESA brightness control (specification not widely implemented). The backlog has decreased from 350 to 316 pending commits, showing progress in clearing old review requests.

recent_posts.title: FOSDEM 2026
recent_posts.summary: FOSDEM 2026 is a free community event for open source developers taking place January 31 - February 1, 2026 in Brussels. Haiku OS won't have a booth this year but will host a Birds of a Feather session on Sunday at 10am discussing what's missing in Haiku for daily driver use, including hardware support, features, documentation, and accessibility.

recent_posts.title: Haiku Activity & Contract Report, December 2025
recent_posts.summary: Haiku OS development activity for December 2025 included improvements across applications (Terminal hyperlink support, MediaPlayer playlist fixes, HiDPI fixes in ProcessController), drivers (updated FreeBSD 15 ethernet/WiFi drivers, Elantech touchpad improvements), file systems (BFS timestamp handling, FAT double-lock fix), and kernel components (network booting in EFI loader, TCP RST handling, memory leak fixes). Notable additions include an EFI loader installation tool in the Installer and basic ARM serial output fixes. The beta6 release is approaching with remaining regressions being addressed.
